Pensacola Mom’s Ultimate Guide to Blues at the Beach

By
Pensacola Mom Collective
-
June 20, 2026
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
Email
    This article is sponsored by Children's Art Classes Pensacola.
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 5:50
    Instaread

    Red, White, and Blues — Pensacola Beach’s beloved annual airshow featuring the world-famous U.S. Navy Blue Angels — earns top billing among locals and vacationers alike.

    This year’s show and related events take place July 15-18, 2026, on Pensacola Beach.

    Because of its popularity, strategic planning is a must — whether you’re going solo, as a couple, with friends, or with family. The Pensacola Mom team has gathered our best tips to help you enjoy the show like a pro!

    This article is made possible by our friends at Children’s Art Classes Pensacola. 

    Children’s Art Classes Pensacola delivers a premier, curriculum-based fine arts program designed to help children build real skills, confidence, and creative mastery. The studio offers a sequential, year-round curriculum that guides students through drawing, painting, sculpture, pottery, mixed media, and more—developing abilities step by step. Parents choose CAC Pensacola because it provides more than “craft time”; it offers a proven educational pathway that nurtures talent and supports long-term growth. With small classes, individualized instruction, and over 40 mediums explored, Children’s Art Classes Pensacola is where young artists learn, thrive, and truly grow.

    Follow Children’s Art Classes Pensacola on Facebook and Instagram. 

    The Easy (But Pricier) Route

    If you’re short on time and want front-row seats with fewer crowds, consider Breakfast With The Blues at Casino Beach Bar & Grill. While this year’s event may already be sold out, it’s never too early to plan for next year. This ticketed event (pricing ranges from $28 – $60+) takes place on Wednesday, before the main show, when parking is still manageable.

    It’s a great option for those who don’t want to commit an entire day to the airshow.

    The Practice Show

    Want to avoid the biggest crowds? The Thursday 2 p.m. practice show is your best bet. Parking is still tricky, but far easier than Friday or Saturday. While you’ll miss some of the openers, you’ll still get the full Blue Angels performance — with less time baking in the sun!

    Before You Go: Pack Like a Pro

    Make packing for the show easy and stress-free! Our free printable checklist covers everything from sunscreen to shade to ear protection — so you can focus on fun, not what you forgot at home.

    Click here to download your Blue Angels Beach Day Checklist

    The Big Show

    Go by Boat (Part 1)

    Thursday’s practice is also ideal for boating. The water is less crowded, so you can easily anchor near Little Sabine or between Quietwater Beach and Sharp Point. If boating Friday or Saturday, bring an extra anchor to avoid drifting, leave early to beat the boat traffic, and expect to walk your boat into position.

    No boat day is complete without steamed shrimp from Joe Patti’s or chicken tenders from Publix — grab your provisions the day before!

    Go by Boat (Part 2)

    Or skip the hassle altogether: TAKE THE FERRY! Board at downtown Pensacola and enjoy a scenic ride to Pensacola Beach. Once docked, hop on the beach shuttle to Casino Beach or the Boardwalk. After the show, shuttle back to the ferry terminal for a stress-free return — no car traffic, just smooth sailing (well, maybe a little boat traffic).

    Watch From a Friend’s House

    If you’re lucky enough to snag an invite to a friend’s beach house or condo, go early to secure parking. Bring snacks or drinks as a thank-you, and consider hanging out at a nearby restaurant until showtime so you’re not imposing too long. Then, return to watch from a balcony, yard, or the sand — with easy restroom access and good company.

    Time your departure: leave right after the show to beat traffic, or plan to linger until the roads clear.

    Before You Pack: Stress-Free Snacks & Lunches

    Don’t get caught without snacks! Our free printable checklist helps you plan the perfect beach-friendly lunch and snack spread — whether you’re boating, picnicking, or sharing with friends. No hangry kids (or grown-ups) on your watch!

    Click here to download your Beach Day Lunch & Snack Checklist

    Favorite Vantage Points by Land

    The best land-based viewing spot? Near the Pensacola Beach Pier — but it is also the most crowded. In past years, Casino Beach Bar has offered reserved seating (for a fee). With that incredible view, you also get a nice table for viewing, bathroom access, and refreshments.

    Consider a resort pass from a Pensacola Beach hotel for Thursday, as it is typically less crowded. Enjoy all the amenities, rent beach chairs, and have a stress-free day — just pack sunscreen and beach essentials!

    Shoreline Park or the National Seashore in Gulf Breeze both offer decent views and easier access, especially for families with young kids.

    Hotels

    If you want to stay beachfront for the long weekend, book a year in advance. A condo or hotel room with a balcony provides the ultimate setup: shade, restrooms, shelter from sun or rain, and zero traffic worries. It’s not cheap — but the memories? Priceless.

    Bonus Tips

    • Parking: Drop a car off near Flounder’s the night before, or pay for parking the day of — it’s worth it to avoid an ultra-early arrival.

    • Noise protection: Bring earplugs or headphones for kids or sound-sensitive adults.

    • Souvenirs: Check out Artesana or Rusted Arrow downtown, Pizzaz in Gulf Breeze, or the Naval Aviation Museum for unique mementos.

    However you choose to experience Red, White, and Blues, a little planning goes a long way toward creating a fun, memorable day. Whether you’re boating, beaching, or cheering from a balcony, we hope these tips — and our free checklists — help take the stress out of your Blue Angels adventure!

    Stay safe, stay hydrated, and soak up the magic of this Pensacola tradition!

    Have a tip of your own for enjoying the show? Share it with us in the comments — we’d love to hear how your family celebrates the Blue Angels!
